newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end mostly higher.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed mostly higher on Wednesday, reflecting price gains on the Chicago market and the weaker yen against the dollar, traders said.
Prices were 70 to 150 yen higher, with the benchmark January 1998 contract up 70 yen at 15,600 yen per tonne. The exception was the spot March, which lost 280 yen to 16,990 yen by the close.
Local investors, encouraged by the stronger Chicago market overnight, actively bought from the opening, traders said.
"Local investors still remember the price surges in world corn markets last year," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot March contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.72 per bushel at 0720 GMT, against $2.72-1/2 at Tuesday's close.
The spot March of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.49-1/2 at 0720 GMT, against $7.49-3/4 at Tuesday's close. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-7391
